angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 305,412 km at 10.00 pc = 0.41 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 100.0232 +/- 0.0208 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 10.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.439 +/- 0.003 solar radii from Luque et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 260655 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...664A.199L/abstract): 305,412 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.439 +/- 0.011 solar masses from Luque et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 260655 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...664A.199L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3803 +/- 10 K from Luque et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 260655 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...664A.199L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Luque et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 260655 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...664A.199L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-260655.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.796, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
